provenance.notes: Exercises every exact default at once: 4-bit integer weights, k=1, ReLU, column-wise scales, dense routing, and the raw uint8-packed weight layout.
Descending `(logit, expert_index)` ordering with selected-weight normalization: equal logits select expert 1, whose output is [16, 32], rather than the all-zero expert 0.
Covers 8-bit integer weights and the supported interleaved SwiGLU mode with non-default alpha and beta.
Two complete 16-element quantization blocks on both reductions, with two selected experts and stable top-k softmax mixing.
Locks the standard rank-3 input form and flattening of batch and sequence into router rows.
Exercises the optional finite SwiGLU clamp and the explicit 8-bit path.

A zero intermediate dimension has an exact zero result without binding empty weight buffers in a shader. No token, routing or scale value can reach the result once the intermediate width is zero, so the fill values are uniform.
Zero tokens in the rank-2 form must retain the routed quantized shader identities while every output dispatch is elided.
A 128-element reduction on both projections exercises the cooperative multi-lane schedule for q4 weights.
Interleaved SwiGLU with two selected experts over a 128-long reduction and four 32-wide quantization blocks per row.
Eight-bit codes over the same 128-long reduction: one stored word per logical column instead of a shared nibble pair.

An 8-bit decode on the cooperative GEMV schedule with an ODD hidden size. The reduction steps two columns at a time -- one stored word per column at 8 bits, one word for both at 4 -- so an odd length leaves a final column that only 8-bit weights can produce.
Enough routed slots per expert to fill grouped tiles, so one dequantized weight tile is reused across a tile of slots.
Enough routed slots per expert to fill grouped tiles, so one dequantized weight tile is reused across a tile of slots.
Three experts share 64 routed slots across 32-row tiles, so most lanes address padding and the store guard discards more rows than it writes.

Enough routed slots per expert fill grouped tiles, allowing each dequantized weight tile to serve several slots. The tolerance covers f32 reassociation in the tiled reduction while remaining far below a 10% error on outputs near 0.4.

Cooperative quantized weight staging across partial 64-column output tiles and routed row tails, with 4/8-bit codes and column/block scales. Small deterministic inputs keep the strict f32 tolerance meaningful.
